what: Read-only check of the floor A/B (F) premise: are our buyer deals bunched just above the .30 floor? Output of floor_dist_20261109.py run at 11-09 14:16 KST on .market/buyer-deals, plus the 14:12 KST board row and the floor derivation. Aggregates only.
decision: F shelved (never installed): 23.7% of the last 24 h deals are in [.30,.32), against the 50% bar; new deals average .361, above Saved .294, so every new deal raises Saved and deal volume is the lever.
share_basis: 1 - price / value_at_purchase; a useless deal counts -1 and a refunded one 0. value_at_purchase equals the catalog list price for every deal, so both bases give the same figures.

board_vs_local_at_14_12_kst.gap: 4 deals and 3.9 share points: about 3 breaks the board counts as -1 that local records had not matched yet, or deals not yet written locally (they are written in batches). Not settled without a ledger read.

floor.base: buyer_support.json discount_floor.floor .30; discount_floor.py falls back to .25 only when the setting is missing or invalid. Fault rates: DEFAULT_RATES (logs/rank-analysis/fault-rates-20261106.json).
floor.derived_uses: An unstated grade counts as the worst allowed. deal_limit: each turn's limit is min(budget, floor(list x (1 - required))). The standing ask must be at most that ceiling. Counters' surplus check uses required_down. Selection (r3_selection.select) caps at ceiling(list, least_required), the best allowed grade. Shop ranking (expected_discount) uses only the fault rate and the food-C penalty, not the floor.

projection: With new deals at mean .361: Saved .296 after about 85 more deals and .309 after about 790 (16-20 h at 40-49 deals/h). The earlier '.33 at the deadline' figure is an end point: (806 + .35 x 6,246) / (2,740 + 6,246) = .333.
